tasks.short: Schedule classes around rooms, trucks, instructors and shifts.

today.trigger: A batch of forklift, VCA or food-safety certificates is nearing expiry in Studytube, a group of new hires has a start date in AFAS, or a site manager asks for a class.
steps: Export who is due from Studytube and who has just started from AFAS, including site and contract.
Check instructor calendars in Outlook and the room and truck list held in Excel or on SharePoint.
Ask Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo which shifts can release people, then wait for replies.
Move names between Studytube, Outlook and the spreadsheet until one date still works.
Send the invites, tell the managers, and rebook anyone who is absent, on nights, or already booked.
drudgery: Copying the same names between Studytube, Excel and Outlook.
Chasing three sites for a reply on who may leave the floor.
Rebuilding a whole session because one instructor or one reach truck was already taken.
today.time_sinks: Most of the hours go on waiting for replies and on rebooking, not on choosing the plan.

lenses.faster: Matching expiry lists, free/busy and room capacity in one pass removes the copy-paste between Studytube, Excel and Outlook and the mail chase that follows.
lenses.autonomous: A night job can open a draft when a Studytube certificate enters a 60-day window or AFAS records a start date, with no reminder in someone's calendar.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort every expiring certificate, including flex workers in the peak season, would have a seat before the expiry week on all three sites.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss the chase and the room spreadsheet. What is left is judging a real clash with a peak outbound day.
lenses.options: Each run can show three feasible plans, such as one class per site, a shared Tilburg and Venlo day, and an early or late slot, each with the headcount taken off each shift.
lenses.altitude: The specialist stops building each timetable and maintains the rules: capacities, instructor qualifications, blackout days and the CAO code for training hours.
reach: The HR administrator's room bookings, Outlook invites and Studytube enrolments for standard sessions.
The site supervisor's first pass at who can leave a shift, once the roster and the rules are both data.
A list of paid training hours the payroll specialist can code from the approved session register.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which Friday in Rotterdam must not lose the outbound crew, and which instructor may teach a reach truck rather than only a counterbalance.
tasks.pattern_why: Who needs which class, and which room, truck and instructor are free, is a set of rules with a checkable result: no double booking, capacity held, every due person seated or listed as overflow. A solver does that without a language model. A person still releases the plan, because it takes people off a shift and training time sits under the CAO.

in_practice.trigger: A Studytube certificate enters a 60-day expiry window, AFAS records a start date with required certificates, or a manager submits a class request.
steps: Read who is due, their site and their contract type from Studytube and AFAS, and flex names from the agency order where the site requires the certificate.
Read instructor and room free/busy from Outlook and equipment capacity from the SharePoint list.
Build sessions that respect capacity, qualification, site and the blackout dates L&D maintains.
Show who would leave which shift, and who still has no seat.
After approval, create the Outlook invites and the Studytube enrolments.
in_practice.human_gate: The L&D specialist approves every run before invites go out, and the site supervisor confirms any session that takes more than the agreed number of people off one shift.
systems: A constraint scheduler built on those exports
data_needed: Certificate expiry, course and validity from Studytube
Employee site, contract and weekly hours from AFAS
Flex workers on site whose certificate the hirer must arrange
Instructor qualifications and Outlook free/busy
Room and truck capacity, and shift blackout dates
The CAO rule for whether the hour is paid working time
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint schedule log storing the rule version and the approval, plus the Studytube enrolment for each person.

evidence.claim: Outlook Scheduling Assistant shows free/busy for people and for rooms that are set up as room mailboxes.
Studytube holds enrolments, completions and expiry dates for mandatory certificates such as forklift, VCA and food safety.
A constraint solver can build a feasible class plan from capacity, qualification and blackout rules when those inputs are data rather than mail.
Shift rosters in Dutch warehouses often sit outside the HR system, so a scheduler that only reads HR records double-books peak shifts.

risks: If the live roster sits in a site spreadsheet or a planner's head, the plan will take people who are already on the outbound shift.
Flex workers live in the agency portals, so a run that only reads AFAS misses people the site still has to instruct.
CAO rules on paid training time, and any works council agreement on working hours, will be broken if they are not written into the rules.
Calendars and absence are AVG data; the run should use free/busy and shift codes, for the purpose of training logistics only.
A later change that ranks who may attend from performance or verzuim would move into employment decision territory under the EU AI Act.
research_questions: In the last quarter of forklift and VCA sessions, what share was rebooked, and was the cause the roster, the instructor, or the room?
Are shift rosters for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo in AFAS at least three weeks ahead, or only on site spreadsheets?
Does the current Studytube subscription already include session planning that nobody uses?
Which CAO clause and which works council agreement decide that a training hour is worked time, and who may approve a release off a shift?

tasks.short: Report monthly training cost and explain the movements.

today.trigger: Month close, a budget question from the HR Director or the controller, or a vendor invoice that does not match what L&D expected.
steps: Pull actuals from AFAS for the training cost centres and chase invoices coded somewhere else.
Add payroll hours for paid training time and the Studytube licence, usually in a separate Excel tab.
Compare the total with last month's workbook and with the budget the controller holds.
Rewrite the same variance explanations: timing, a late invoice, or a course that ran twice.
Send the workbook to finance and answer the same questions again in Teams.
drudgery: Rebuilding the monthly workbook from an AFAS export and VLOOKUP.
Splitting one Studytube invoice across three sites by a homemade key.
Hunting invoices that were coded to a warehouse cost centre instead of training.
today.time_sinks: The hours sit in reconciling sources that do not share a key, and in explaining differences that are often just timing or a wrong cost centre.

lenses.faster: The export, the VLOOKUP and the reformat disappear once ledger accounts, payroll wage types and the Studytube licence map to one training table.
lenses.autonomous: On the night the AFAS extract refreshes Power BI, the training table updates and flags any line that crossed an agreed euro or percent threshold.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort every programme would show cost per completion and cost per person still in the job 90 days after hire or after a move, which the company does not see today.
lenses.joy: Coding invoices and rebuilding the workbook is the part nobody will miss. Judging whether an external trainer in Venlo is worth the rate is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: The same actuals can be cut by site, by permanent staff and flex, by mandatory certificate and elective course, and as a year-end forecast under a high and a low hiring month.
lenses.altitude: The specialist stops assembling the workbook and owns the definitions: what counts as a training euro, which wage types are in, and which exceptions the controller has already accepted.
reach: The FP&A analyst's rebuild of the training lines during month close.
The controller's first-pass variance questions on the training cost centre.
The people analytics analyst's cost-per-completion figures on the HR dashboard.

tasks.human_edge: Telling a real overrun from a late invoice or a miscode, and deciding whether a programme should stop, shrink, or run again next quarter.
tasks.pattern_why: The report is a join of AFAS ledger lines, payroll wage types and Studytube completions against an agreed budget. The totals are checkable against the ledger. The justification sentence is filled from those computed variances, so a model is not asked to produce a number the controller cannot trace to a journal line.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract lands, and again at month close before the controller locks the period.
steps: Join general-ledger actuals, accounts-payable invoices and payroll training-hour wage types to the agreed training categories.
Attach Studytube completions for the same period and the same course names.
Flag lines over the threshold, new suppliers, and amounts with no matching completion.
Fill a one-page note from those flags: site, programme, amount, and whether it is timing or a true overrun.
File the pack in the same SharePoint place the controller already uses for month-end.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D approves the monthly note before it goes to the HR Director, and the controller approves any change to the account mapping. Corrections are made in AFAS coding, not by typing over the figure.
data_needed: General-ledger actuals and budget by cost centre and period
Supplier and invoice reference from accounts payable
Payroll wage types for CAO paid training time
Studytube completions by course and site
Agency invoice lines that separate training from hours, where the agency can provide them
in_practice.logs_to: The Power BI dataset, with the AFAS period it was built from, and the monthly note stored beside it on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit posts purchase invoices and payroll to the general ledger by cost centre and period, and can hold a budget against those accounts.
Power BI can refresh a model on a schedule from an extract and show budget against actual.
Training spend in logistics companies is usually split across external invoices, paid trainee hours and an LMS licence, so a single general-ledger view undercounts until the mapping is agreed.

risks: Invoices coded to a warehouse cost centre produce a tidy training report that is too low.
Paid time on a course often sits in payroll, and flex training often sits inside a single agency invoice, so a vendor-only view overstates external trainers.
A justification the controller cannot click through to an AFAS journal line will be set aside.
Person-level training cost is AVG data; the monthly pack should stay at site and programme unless finance has a stated purpose and a retention rule.
research_questions: What share of last year's training invoices in AFAS accounts payable was coded outside the training cost centres?
Which payroll wage types mark CAO paid training time, and are they already in the nightly extract that feeds Power BI?
Can the three staffing agencies split training from hours on their invoices, or is flex training invisible in the weekly total?
How many hours a month does this pack take now, and how much of that is rebuilding Excel rather than discussing a variance?

tasks.short: Design a path from the warehouse floor to team lead.

today.trigger: The HR Director or a site manager says supervisor or team-lead seats are being filled from outside, or the yearly workforce conversation opens.
steps: Ask the HR business partners who on the floor might be ready, and collect names from managers' heads.
Look up the function grid and old leadership slides on SharePoint.
Rewrite a generic programme in PowerPoint that assumes people can leave the shift for full days.
Negotiate one cohort onto a classroom calendar and watch attendance fail for night shifts.
Hear later, informally, whether the people who moved are coping.
drudgery: Rewriting the same competency slides under a new title.
Chasing nominations by mail from managers who are on shift.
Copying function descriptions out of SharePoint into a workbook nobody opens.
today.time_sinks: The time goes into slide work and into finding a day three sites can attend. Almost none of it goes into checking whether the people who stepped up are effective after 90 days.

lenses.faster: The first outlines, the practice cases from a real shift, and the side-by-side comparison of time off the floor can be drafted in a sitting, so the specialist spends the hours with HR business partners and site managers.
lenses.autonomous: A quarterly pull of open supervisor vacancies from Recruitee and of internal moves from AFAS can open the design round without waiting for a director to remember. The programme itself stays led by a person.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the design cost Noordhaven would keep a small bench of future team leads on each site, matched to vacancies that are actually open, and would measure who is still effective 90 days into the role.
lenses.joy: Rewriting competency slides is the part that can go. The conversations with someone who wants to run a shift, and with the crew that would work for them, are the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Five shapes can sit side by side: a buddy period with a duty manager, short Studytube modules plus floor practice, a single-site pilot, a version for office planners, and a version limited to feedback and verzuim conversations.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets what 'ready for team lead' means, how someone enters, and how a cohort is judged at 90 days, and stops hand-building each year's slides.
reach: The HR business partner's preparation for a succession conversation, with the decision left in that room.
The recruiter's choice to hold a supervisor vacancy for someone already on the path.
The compensation and benefits check of which function group a completed path maps to under the CAO.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing who a night shift will actually follow, who wants the job, and what the works council and the function grid will accept. Selection and the coaching conversation stay with the manager and the specialist.
tasks.pattern_why: Devising the path is a series of judgments with the HR Director, the HR business partners, site managers and the works council. A model can draft pathways, floor cases and the hours off shift. It should not decide who has potential, and it cannot say what the works council will consent to. The specialist stays the lead.

in_practice.trigger: A cluster of supervisor or team-lead vacancies appears in Recruitee, or the yearly workforce talk with the HR Director is scheduled.
steps: Pull internal moves, time in the new role, and open supervisor vacancies from AFAS and Recruitee.
Draft three paths that fit shift patterns and the function grid, each with hours off the floor and a cost line from the training budget.
Rewrite the path that matches how the sites actually run, with the HR business partners.
Agree nomination rules a manager can explain in person, with every name chosen by a manager.
Place the modules in Studytube and review completions and 90-day outcomes after the first cohort.
in_practice.human_gate: The HR Director approves the path before anyone is nominated. The works council is consulted before it becomes a standing training rule. Every nomination is a manager's decision, recorded as such.
data_needed: Function groups and the step from operator or planner to team lead
Supervisor vacancies and how they were filled
Internal move dates and whether the person is still in the role at 90 days
Training hours and budget by site
Nomination criteria a manager can apply without a score from a model
in_practice.logs_to: The programme file on SharePoint, and a small outcome table (cohort, site, role, still in seat at 90 days) built from AFAS.

evidence.claim: Recruitee already holds vacancies and pipeline stages, so supervisor openings and whether they were filled are listed there.
AFAS Profit holds the employee's function and contract history, which is enough to count internal moves and time in the new role.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can draft a programme outline and practice cases from notes and a function description the specialist supplies, for the specialist to edit.
An AI system used to rank people for promotion falls under the employment provisions of the EU AI Act and needs a human decision, a stated purpose under the AVG, and a data-protection assessment.

risks: A draft written in generic leadership language will be ignored by people who run a shift in Venlo or on nights in Rotterdam.
Scoring potential from verzuim, speed or manager notes is a promotion decision: it needs an AVG purpose, and under the EU AI Act an AI ranking for promotion is high-risk.
A path that implies a higher CAO function group, before compensation and benefits and the works council have agreed, creates pay expectations.
Putting agency staff on a leadership path can be heard as a promise of employment that the agency contract does not contain.
Classroom days will keep failing while the cohort is on a two-shift or three-shift pattern.
research_questions: How many team-lead and supervisor vacancies in the last two years were filled internally, and how many of those people were still in the role after 90 days?
Does a function grid or the warehouse CAO already define the step from operator to team lead, or is that definition the real work?
Will the works council treat this path as a training regulation that needs consent, and has the OR clerk already been asked?
Which data would a nomination use, and has anyone already blocked the use of verzuim or performance notes for selection?

tasks.short: Develop short training on waste, damage and fuel use.

today.trigger: A site manager complains about damage or waste, a customer asks what the crews are taught, or someone remembers the yearly environment slides.
steps: Find last year's PowerPoint on SharePoint, often written for one site only.
Ask finance whether damage, waste or fuel even has a number, and wait.
Rewrite a general session that tries to cover recycling, driving and the dock in one hour.
Deliver it once in Rotterdam; Tilburg and Venlo get a shortened retell.
Do not check whether damage or waste moved afterwards.
drudgery: Searching SharePoint for the last version of a deck nobody owns.
Rewriting generic sustainability slides that do not mention a Noordhaven dock.
Chasing attendance lists after a toolbox talk that was never written down.
today.time_sinks: The few hours go into making a deck and getting one room booked. None of them go into a before-and-after look at damage or waste.

lenses.faster: A first script and a short quiz can be drafted from the site procedure and last quarter's damage or waste figure, so the specialist's time goes to checking it on the floor.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly breach of an agreed damage or waste threshold on the finance extract can open a draft toolbox script. Someone still has to give the talk at the start of the shift.
lenses.ambitious: Done properly for the first time, each site would run one ten-minute talk tied to its own damage or waste figure, and L&D would look at that figure again eight weeks later.
lenses.joy: The generic slide deck is the part nobody will miss. Walking the dock and picking the one behaviour people will follow with gloves on is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Five ten-minute talks, on wrap waste, forklift battery care, loading damage, dock sorting and engine idling, can be drafted from the same procedure so the site picks the one that matches its number.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the rule for how a site figure becomes a ten-minute talk, and checks whether that figure moved, instead of writing a new course from scratch each year.
reach: The controller's damage and waste lines, turned into a talk a site manager can run at shift start.
The HR business partner's evidence when a customer asks which crews were trained and on which version of the procedure.

tasks.human_edge: Seeing which waste is real on a night shift, and signing that the talk does not contradict the VCA rules or the food-safety procedure already in force on that site.
tasks.pattern_why: The procedure and the cost line can feed a draft script and a quiz, and each quiz item can be checked back to a sentence in the procedure. Choosing the one behaviour, confirming it is safe next to VCA and food safety, and having it given on a shift, stays with the specialist and the site manager.

in_practice.trigger: Damage or waste cost on the AFAS extract crosses a threshold the controller agrees, a customer asks for proof of training, or the yearly check of the module comes due.
steps: Read the current site procedure on SharePoint and the last months of damage or waste cost from the finance extract.
Draft a ten-minute toolbox script and a short Studytube quiz that quote the procedure.
Have the site manager and L&D strike anything that conflicts with VCA or food safety.
Deliver it on one shift per site and record who attended.
Read the same cost line eight weeks later before writing anything new.
in_practice.human_gate: The site manager and the L&D specialist both approve the script before it is used. It becomes mandatory only if the HR Director decides so, after the works council is consulted where the change is a standing work instruction.
data_needed: The current waste, damage or fuel procedure on SharePoint
Damage, waste or fuel cost by site from the finance extract
VCA and food-safety instructions the script must not contradict
Attendance by session and site
in_practice.logs_to: The script version stored on SharePoint next to the procedure, and the Studytube completion or the attendance list for the toolbox talk.

evidence.claim: Studytube can publish a short module with a quiz and record who completed it.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can draft a short document from a procedure the user opens in SharePoint, for a person to edit before anyone uses it.

On a warehouse floor, a ten-minute talk at shift start is more likely to change a handling habit than a yearly e-learning course, and the effect is visible only if a cost line is read again afterwards.
Damage and residual-waste costs are often already booked in the ledger as write-offs or claims, so a finance extract can supply the outcome line if the accounts are identifiable.

risks: A talk written from a generic model can contradict the site's VCA or food-safety procedure, which is worse than no talk.
Without a damage or waste line that finance already trusts, the module becomes another Studytube item with a completion rate and no result.
Tracking who failed to recycle, person by person, would be workplace monitoring and needs an AVG purpose; a crew-level cost line does not.
Making the talk mandatory, or changing how people must work, can be a matter for the works council if it becomes a standing instruction.
This is a small, low-frequency task; a heavy build will cost more than the hours it replaces.
research_questions: Is there a SharePoint procedure for waste, damage or fuel, and when did a shift last work to it?
Does the AFAS finance extract already show damage, residual waste or claims by site, in accounts L&D would be allowed to read?
Do customers or management actually ask for this training, or is the demand only the general task description?
Does a ten-minute talk fit the start of a shift on each site, and who is allowed to give it?

role.altitude: The two L&D specialists stop being the people who chase calendars, rebuild the training workbook and rewrite slides. They run the training system: the rules for who must sit a class, the definitions of a training euro, the paths into team lead, and the check that a person is productive and still here 90 days later.
reach: HR administrator: standard enrolments, certificate reminders and session admin across the three sites.
Recruiter: the week-one learning plan for a new hire, tied to the start date in Recruitee and the contract in AFAS.
People analytics and HRIS analyst: training measures on the nightly Power BI extract, including completion, time to certificate and still-in-seat at 90 days.
HR business partner: the refresher a team lead uses in a return-to-work conversation under the Wet verbetering poortwachter, with the case file and the conversation staying with the partner.
FP&A analyst and controller: the monthly training cost note inside the close they already run.
Payroll specialist: a checked list of paid training hours ready before the pay run.
Compensation and benefits specialist: which completed path maps to which CAO function group, as input to grading.
role.ceiling_note: These four tasks are about 220 hours a year per FTE, roughly one seventh of the role. The rest is delivery on shifts, coaching, certificate judgment and works-council consultation, across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, and two people cannot be on three sites at once. Mandatory certificates and any choice of who may enter a leadership path stay with a person because of liability, the AVG and the works council. Dirty rosters, miscoded cost centres and flex workers who are not in AFAS cap how far an unattended run can go.
skills_to_grow: Write scheduling rules a solver can run: capacity, instructor qualification, blackout days and the CAO code for a training hour.
Trace a training euro from an AFAS journal line to a Studytube completion and explain the gap to the controller.
Shape a team-lead path inside the function grid and prepare it for a works council consent conversation.
Recognise when a learning recommendation has become a selection or monitoring decision under the AVG and the EU AI Act.
Turn one site figure into a ten-minute toolbox talk a supervisor will actually give at the start of a shift.
role.ambitious_version: L&D becomes the way Noordhaven raises the share of open roles filled by someone who is productive and still here after 90 days. Every forklift, VCA and food-safety certificate is seated before it expires, including flex workers in the busy months. Every training euro is tied to a completion and, where it matters, to that 90-day outcome. Supervisor vacancies are held long enough for someone grown from the floor to be ready. The two specialists spend their time on the cohorts, the works council and the exceptions the sites will not bend.
